payload.detail: line_green moved relative to gripper while held

payload.explanation: Monitor mon_0489e935b0cc (clause: in-hand slippage, threshold_source raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m=0.02) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792455503990136800 with observed relative tcp->line_green displacement 0.0203 m, just over the 0.02 m slip tolerance. get_evidence over the surrounding window (1792455503e9-1792455505e9) on object_poses(line_green) and frames(tcp) shows line_green's world pose essentially stationary (x/y/z moving <0.0005 m total) while the tcp frame continued descending by about 0.011 m (z: 0.1391->0.1283) during the final lowering move_grasp_center_to_pose toward the placement pose. That pattern -- the held part's world position staying fixed while the gripper continues to travel -- means the part was arrested, almost certainly by contact with the placement feature/fixture, while the gripper kept closing the commanded final offset, producing genuine relative motion between tcp and part inside the gripper. This is a real physical event, not a mis-armed monitor: the transform(tcp,line_green) reading is a direct, correctly-computed measure of the quantity the invariant specifies. The specification states the in-hand slippage invariant must hold throughout the hold with no carve-out for contact during seating, so the measured 0.0203 m exceeds the declared 0.02 m tolerance and is recorded as a violation of that invariant, even though it is a mild, contact-induced settling rather than a dropped or grossly mis-held part. The breach is marginal (1.5% over threshold) and I could not identify any specification language exempting compliant seating contact, so I did not treat it as a valid_variation.

payload.summary: u_brown (already seated at its milestone, inactive during place_line_green) rotated by roughly 5.7 degrees in place between wall_ns 1792455502185293800 and 1792455504485803000 (orientation w: 0.7071 -> 0.6795), coincident with line_green's placement contact and the in-hand-slip fire on line_green. Its position barely changed (within the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance), so the position-based disturbance monitor did not fire, but the orientation shift itself is unaccounted for by any step acting on u_brown.
payload.impact_detail: No raw_spec field defines an orientation-based disturbance tolerance for an already-seated part (only disturbance_tolerance_m, position-only, is specified), so this rotation cannot be adjudicated against a contract threshold and is not recorded as a clause failure. It is flagged because it is physically consistent with contact transmitted through the fixture/line_green during that part's placement, and because u_brown's final orientation must still be checked against u_brown_placement at run end.

payload.explanation: Monitor mon_9dae9dc7c4a2 (clause: Undisturbed objects - u_brown is now seated and inactive, threshold raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m=0.02) fired at trigger_wall_ns=1792455704788252000 with u_brown having moved 0.0236 m from its seated baseline, during place_inverted_u_yellow (which names only inverted_u_yellow in object_ids; u_brown was not acted on by this step). get_evidence over object_poses for u_brown and inverted_u_yellow across 1792455700e9-1792455706e9 shows the cause directly: inverted_u_yellow descends toward its placement (z: 0.124 -> 0.061 m over this window, x/y converging toward ~0.40,-0.197) while, starting at wall_ns 1792455703935531500, u_brown's pose stops being static and begins oscillating -- position jumps from (0.4023,-0.1512,0.0430) to (0.4066,-0.1511,0.0439) and briefly to z=0.0665 at wall_ns 1792455704935419100, with its orientation quaternion swinging from w~0.707 to w~0.73 and back -- before settling again near (0.4058,-0.1515,0.0479) by the end of the window. This start-stop timing lines up with inverted_u_yellow's carried descent passing close to u_brown's seated position, so the mechanism is a part-on-part contact: the carried inverted_u_yellow struck or brushed the already-seated u_brown while being lowered into place, physically displacing it beyond the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance before it came back to rest nearby. u_brown was inactive at this point (its own place_u_brown milestone had already closed), so this is a standing-requirement violation, not something excused by inverted_u_yellow's own effects due here. This also plausibly explains the earlier recorded orientation shift of u_brown observed during place_line_green (obs-001-1be7f625): u_brown appears to be sitting close enough to the other placement frames that it is vulnerable to repeated incidental contact as later parts are carried in and seated.

This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all twelve steps observed (all on the expected process map; none unplanned). I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame from my own query_snapshot at run end, independent of the executor's claim_detail: u_brown vs u_brown_placement = 0.00217 m (tol 0.01), u_orange vs u_orange_placement = 0.0023 m (tol 0.02), line_green vs line_green_placement = 0.01023 m (tol 0.015), inverted_u_yellow vs inverted_u_yellow_placement = 0.00243 m (tol 0.012) -- all four within tolerance, with correct orientation (largest orientation error 3.2 deg vs 10 deg tolerance) and correct grasp width/effort/lift-height effects at each part's own place step. base1 and every bystander (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) remain at their original poses to within noise; base1 itself drifted ~0.0029 m (well inside its 0.02 m reference tolerance), which also explains why the published placement frames shifted a few mm in world coordinates between early and late snapshots -- they ride on base1's TF chain, not an independent error.

Two findings were recorded during the run. (1) At place_line_green, monitor mon_0489e935b0cc fired for in-hand slippage: tcp-to-line_green relative displacement reached 0.0203 m, just over the 0.02 m grasp_slip_tolerance_m, at the exact moment object_poses/frames evidence shows line_green's world pose freeze while tcp continued descending -- consistent with the part contacting its seat while the gripper kept closing the commanded offset. (2) At place_inverted_u_yellow, monitor mon_9dae9dc7c4a2 fired because the already-seated, inactive u_brown moved 0.0236 m from its resting baseline; get_evidence showed u_brown oscillating in both position and orientation for about a second while inverted_u_yellow was being carried down into its own placement, in the same region of the bench -- a part-on-part contact between the carried inverted_u_yellow and the seated u_brown. Both findings are real physical events, not mis-armed monitors, and are recorded as non_conformant verdicts under their own step_ids.

Neither violation stands at run end: u_brown's final pose is 0.00217 m from u_brown_placement (it settled back into tolerance after the contact), and line_green's final pose is 0.01155 m from line_green_placement (the brief in-hand compliance at contact did not carry it out of tolerance). I also carried an open observation (obs-001-1be7f625) noting an earlier, smaller orientation shift of u_brown during place_line_green that could not be adjudicated against any orientation-based disturbance threshold (the registry only defines a position-based disturbance_tolerance_m) -- this is consistent with, and likely an earlier instance of, the same bystander-proximity contact pattern that produced the place_inverted_u_yellow finding, but it never exceeded a defined bound on its own.

Because every part's final pose is within tolerance of its placement frame, no violation stands at run end, and both mid-run findings were followed by the affected part returning to tolerance, the run's end-state is conformant -- a recovery from two transient contact-induced disturbances, not a clean run, but a correct one at termination. I was unable to independently recompute the contract's exact object_tcp_offset_m geometric definition (it depends on an internal grasp-center-offset transform not exposed to me); I used the raw tcp-to-held-object relative-transform drift (the same signal used for the in-hand-slippage invariant) as the best available proxy for grasp tracking consistency at each part's pick step, and it stayed within the slip tolerance except for the one recorded line_green fire.
